vector, which represents the power per unit area carried by the wave. In a medium with an
index of refraction of 1.5, the speed of light is reduced, but the electric field
amplitude remains a critical parameter for calculating the Poynting vector. Given an
electric field amplitude of 100 volts/meter, the magnitude of the Poynting vector can be
calculated using the formula \( S = \frac{1}{\mu_0 c} E^2 \), where \( \mu_0 \) is the
permeability of free space and \( c \) is the speed of light in a vacuum. Substituting the
values, we find that the Poynting vector has a magnitude of approximately 19.9 W/m^2. This
value signifies the average power flow per unit area of the light wave as it propagates
through the glass, highlighting how energy is transmitted through the medium.
